title: I Followed the Stained-Glass Kiln Booking Into the Shelf They Took

parts.text: I loaded shelf C at 1:44 p.m. and mentor Lumen had already slid a private piece onto my unpaid-looking leftover fire. The calendar said: BOOK THE KILN. LOG THE SHELF. NO PRIVATE ADDS. I was thirty-five, member, holding a hold slip. Lumen shrugged. "Mentors are the fire." I photographed the calendar, the slip, and the extra piece. Then I logged an overlap. At 1:51 the studio lead pinged why Lumen's name was on my shelf. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio lead can see Lumen's private piece on shelf C during my kiln booking.

social.video_title: The mentor slid a private piece onto my kiln shelf — Part 1/2
social.description: Stained glass, a kiln hold, an extra piece. I logged the overlap. Would you have asked the lead?

parts.text: Lumen called it space until the lead asked for the still. I printed the overlap, the calendar, and the slip. The piece came off. Lumen booked a private fire and told members space was always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when kilns exist. Booking now has a second line: MENTORS LOG THEIR OWN SHELF. I keep shelf C. Lumen schedules. The kiln finally looks like a hold, not leftover glass. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors log their own shelf — Part 2/2
social.description: Overlap log, piece off, and a second line. Was space ever my fire?
